([[Folsom, California]]) | college = * [[Sonoma State Seawolves men's basketball|Sonoma State]] (2021–2023) * [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]] (2023–2024) | highlights = * [[California Collegiate Athletic Association|CCAA]] Player of the Year (2023) * First-team All-CCAA (2023) }} '''Jaylen Wells''' (born August 26, 2003) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Sonoma State Seawolves men's basketball|Sonoma State Seawolves]] and the [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State Cougars]]. ==Early life and high school career== Wells grew up in [[Sacramento, California]] and attended [[Folsom High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/high-school/article262985473.html|title=Trio of young Sacramento players train against pros|first=Joe|last=Davidson|work=[[The Sacramento Bee]]|date=July 10, 2022|access-date=May 14, 2024}} As a senior, he averaged 26.3 points, 3.2 rebounds and 1.2 assists per game. He was named the area Player of the Year by ''[[The Sacramento Bee]]''.{{cite web|url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/high-school/article252297233.html|title=Bee's Best Basketball Players of the Year, Harriel and Wells|work=[[The Sacramento Bee]]|date=July 7, 2021|access-date=May 14, 2024}} Wells committed to play [[college basketball]] at [[NCAA Division II|Division II]] [[Sonoma State University]].{{cite web|url=https://goldcountrymedia.com/news/189808/jaylen-wells-can-do-it-all-on-the-court/|title=Jaylen Wells can do it all on the court|first=Matt|last=Long|work=Gold Country Media|date=May 27, 2021|access-date=May 14, 2024}} ==College career== Wells began his college basketball career playing for the [[Sonoma State Seawolves]].{{cite web|url=https://www.pressdemocrat.com/article/sports/college-notebook-former-ssu-star-jaylen-wells-helps-washington-state-to-nc/|title=Former SSU star helps Washington State to NCAA Tournament|first=Gus|last=Morris|work=[[The Press Democrat]]|date=March 21, 2024|access-date=May 13, 2024}} He averaged 12.6 points per game during his freshman season.{{cite web|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2023/apr/18/jaylen-wells-a-division-ii-all-american-from-sonom/|title=Jaylen Wells, a Division II All-American from Sonoma State, transfers to Washington State|work=[[The Spokesman-Review]]|date=April 18, 2023|access-date=May 13, 2024}} Wells was named the [[California Collegiate Athletic Association]] Player of the Year after averaging 22.4 points per game during his sophomore season.{{cite web|url=https://www.pressdemocrat.com/article/sports/college-notebook-ssus-jaylen-wells-named-to-division-ii-all-region-basket/|title=College notebook: SSU's Jaylen Wells named conference Player of the Year|first=Gus|last=Morris|work=[[The Press Democrat]]|date=March 16, 2023|access-date=May 13, 2024}} After the season he entered the NCAA transfer portal.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/washington-state/article/wsu-basketball-jaylen-wells-file-on-6-7-forward-212246970/|title=WSU basketball: The file on 6-7 forward Jaylen Wells|first=Jamey|last=Vinnick|website=[[247Sports]]|date=July 4, 2023|access-date=May 14, 2024}} Wells ultimately transferred to [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]]. He entered his junior season as the Cougars' starting small forward.{{cite web|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/wsu-cougar-basketball/behind-the-transformation-of-wsu-mens-basketball-guard-jaylen-wells-and-his-elite-shooting/|title=Behind the transformation of WSU guard Jaylen Wells, and his elite shooting|work=[[The Seattle Times]]|date=December 16, 2023|access-date=May 13, 2024}} Wells averaged 12.6 points and 4.6 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/washington-state/article/jaylen-wells-wsu-basketball-says-entire-focus-is-on-nba-not-transfer-portal-231235506/|title=WSU's Jaylen Wells says entire focus is on NBA, not transfer portal|first=Jamey|last=Vinnick|website=[[247Sports]]|date=April 30, 2024|access-date=May 13, 2024}} After the season, Wells declared for the [[2024 NBA draft]] while retaining his college eligibility.{{cite web|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2024/apr/04/wsu-wing-jaylen-wells-declares-for-nba-draft-retai/|title=WSU wing Jaylen Wells declares for NBA Draft, retaining option to return to school|first=Greg|last=Woods|work=[[The Spokesman-Review]]|date=April 4, 2024|access-date=May 13, 2024}} He later also re-entered the transfer portal.{{cite web|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/wsu-cougar-basketball/wsu-mens-wing-jaylen-wells-reportedly-entering-transfer-portal/|title=WSU men's wing Jaylen Wells reportedly entering transfer portal|work=[[The Seattle Times]]|date=April 25, 2024|access-date=May 13, 2024}} Wells later decided to remain in the draft.{{cite web|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/wsu-cougar-basketball/former-wsu-wing-jaylen-wells-staying-in-nba-draft-pool/|title=Former WSU wing Jaylen Wells staying in NBA draft
